FIRST, a measurement gap: backtest2 walks one coin at a time with UNLIMITED concurrency, while live caps the whole book at strategy2.MAX_TRADES=2 and ranks same-bar candidates by |stretch| (find_setup). Built portfolio2.py to model the real book on one shared clock. At the deployed setting the gap is harmless -- capped n=116 +36.49% maxDD -12.49% vs uncapped n=121 +33.43% maxDD -14.57% -- which MEASURES the 07-26 claim that concurrency never exceeded 2 rather than asserting it, and validates every backtest2 number quoted so far. It is NOT harmless at higher signal rates: with the ADX gate removed, uncapped reports maxDD -74.33% against the real capped -10.59%. Any frequency question (MAX_ADX, RSI, stretch, more coins) must now be answered in portfolio2, not backtest2. SECOND, the finding: the ADX gate buys no EV. Capped portfolio sim, 20 coins, 5000 bars, fees in, live ratchet semantics -- ADX<20 n=34 EV +0.105% t=0.37; ADX<25 (deployed) n=116 EV +0.315% t=2.13 net +36.49% maxDD -12.49%; ADX<30 n=249 EV +0.249%; ADX<35 n=362 EV +0.211%; ADX<40 n=461 EV +0.297%; NO GATE n=697 EV +0.478% t=6.31 net +333.44% maxDD -10.59%, 7/7 positive months, 16/20 positive coins, ex-top5 +267%, and it survives out-of-sample (older n=372 +245%, newer n=325 +88% t=3.54) and does not depend on the |stretch| ranking (alphabetical selection +284%) or on the cap (cap1 +213%, cap4 +430%). The gate cuts 88.5% of RSI-extreme bars for zero EV gain. This is internally consistent with the 07-30 finding that the ENTRY has no edge (-2.82% at fixed 1R) and the ratchet is the whole system: if the trigger contributes nothing, a regime filter on the trigger cannot contribute either, and more triggers is simply more lottery tickets for the ratchet. S2 is not really a mean-reversion strategy; it is a ratchet harvester with a mean-reversion trigger.
